raw_meta_yaml:
# PRESTO builds BOTH halves from one source: meson builds libpresto + the C
# tools, then pip builds the Python package (which links the just-installed
# libpresto).
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "6.1.0"

package:
  # 'presto' is taken on bioconda by an unrelated tool (immcantation's
  # immunology toolkit), and conda-forge shares that namespace, so this
  # astronomy PRESTO is packaged as 'presto-pulsar'.  The Python import stays
  # 'presto' and the command-line tool names are unchanged.
  name: presto-pulsar
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/scottransom/presto/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 90b600dea4542e442a36184a05d2257781d8ec8b0219808e72e1ed31f01a0d3d

build:
  number: 0
  skip: win

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - meson >=1.3
    - ninja
    - pkg-config
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    # the 'mesonpy' PEP517 backend must import under the host python
    - meson-python
    - numpy
    - fftw
    # conda-forge's global pin is still gsl 2.7 while the gsl 2.8 migration is
    # in flight, but tempo2 (a run dependency) has already been rebuilt against
    # gsl 2.8.  Building against 2.7 would run_export gsl >=2.7,<2.8 and make
    # presto-pulsar impossible to co-install with tempo2, so ask for 2.8 here.
    # Drop this constraint once the global pin moves to 2.8.
    - gsl >=2.8
    - cfitsio
    - glib
    # ERFA, used for barycentering (run_exports pins it into run)
    - liberfa
    - libpng
    - xorg-libx11
    # xproto.pc / kbproto.pc, required by x11.pc at configure time
    - xorg-xorgproto
    # xcb.pc, required (private) by x11.pc
    - libxcb
    - pgplot
    # OpenMP runtime: PRESTO parallelizes rfifind/accelsearch/prepfold, so the
    # tools link libgomp/libomp (run_export pins it into run).
    - if: linux
      then: libgomp
    - if: osx
      then: llvm-openmp
    # BLAS: libpresto links cblas via GSL (DT_NEEDED libopenblas.so.0); use
    # conda-forge's switchable BLAS so its run_export pins the implementation.
    - libblas
    - libcblas
  run:
    - python
    - scipy
    - astropy-base
    - matplotlib-base
    - pgplot
    - xorg-libx11
    # optional: prepfold converts its .ps plots to .png
    - ghostscript
    # polyco generation (prepfold -timing)
    - tempo2

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - presto
        - presto.presto
      pip_check: true
  - script:
      # Run two tools with no args (they print their pyclig usage) to confirm the
      # binaries run and resolve all their shared libs (pgplot, fftw, ...).
      - readfile 2>&1 | grep -qi "raw data"
      - accelsearch 2>&1 | grep -qi "acceleration search"
  - package_contents:
      bin:
        - accelsearch
        - prepfold
        - readfile
      lib:
        - presto
      files:
        - lib/pkgconfig/presto.pc
        - share/presto/pulsars.cat
        - share/presto/psr_catalog.txt
        - share/presto/aliases.txt

about:
  license: GPL-2.0-only
  license_file: COPYING
  summary: PulsaR Exploration and Search TOolkit
  description: |
    PRESTO is a large suite of pulsar search and analysis software.  It was
    primarily designed to efficiently search for binary millisecond pulsars
    from long observations of globular clusters, but has been used in many
    surveys and for X-ray data.  It is written primarily in ANSI C, with many
    higher-level routines in Python.
  homepage: https://github.com/scottransom/presto
  repository: https://github.com/scottransom/presto
  documentation: https://github.com/scottransom/presto/wiki

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - scottransom
